translationRepairs: On the next day, court ranks were advanced one step nationwide, two for those engaged in the funeral, taxes and corvée were waived for a year, and every official from prefect upward received the noble title marquis within the passes.

On the bingzi day, court ranks were advanced one step nationwide, two for those engaged in the funeral, taxes and corvée were waived for a year, and every official from prefect upward received the noble title marquis within the passes.
Chinese 丙子 is a named sexagenary day after 辛未, not the next calendar day.
Grand Commandant Yang Jun was appointed grand tutor to oversee state affairs at the young emperor’s side.
Grand Commandant Yang Jun was appointed grand tutor to oversee state affairs.
The Chinese 輔政 does not describe a young emperor.
In the eighth month, Sima You, prince of Guangling, was named crown prince; He Shao became his grand preceptor, Wang Rong his grand tutor, and Yang Ji his grand guardian.
In autumn, on the renwu day of the eighth month, Sima Yu, prince of Guangling, was named crown prince; He Shao became his grand preceptor, Wang Rong his grand tutor, and Yang Ji his grand guardian.
The personal name 遹 is Yu, not You, and the date omits 秋八月壬午.
With that the edict ended. A further edict forbade imperial clansmen and officials to visit the imperial tombs.
A further edict forbade imperial clansmen and officials to visit the imperial tombs.
The Chinese 又詔 has no clause saying the previous edict ended.
Prince Xiong of Liang was shifted from the eastern to the western theater as area commander beyond the passes, while Ruan Tan was sent to pacify the east and oversee the armies of Qing and Xu.
Prince Rong of Liang was shifted from the eastern to the western theater as area commander beyond the passes, while Ruan Tan was sent to pacify the east and oversee the armies of Qing and Xu.
梁王肜 transcribes as Rong, not Xiong.
Preceptor to Prince You of Guangling, Liu Shi, was made grand guardian of the heir apparent; Minister of Works, Prince Tai of Longxi, recorded the affairs of the secretariat.
Preceptor to the Prince of Guangling, Liu Shi, was made grand guardian of the heir apparent; Minister of Works, Prince Tai of Longxi, recorded the affairs of the secretariat.
廣陵王師 names the office, not a personal name You.
A stone was said to have “sprouted” in Yifang ward inside the capital.
A stone was said to have “sprouted” in Yinian ward inside the capital.
Chinese 宜年里 is Yinian ward; Yifang is a different place-name and is not in the source.
There was a stone that grew in Yifang Ward in the capital.
There was a stone that grew in Yinian Ward in the capital.
Chinese 宜年里 is Yinian, not Yifang.

Prince Lun of Zhao was recalled from the western command to the capital post of general of chariots and cavalry, while Prince Xiong of Liang took his place as general-in-chief in the west with authority over Yong and Liang and a mandate to hold the Guanzhong frontier.

Prince Lun of Zhao was recalled from the western command to the capital post of general of chariots and cavalry, while Prince Rong of Liang took his place as general-in-chief in the west with authority over Yong and Liang and a mandate to hold the Guanzhong frontier.
The prince is 梁王肜 (Rong), the same Liang prince as earlier in the chapter; Xiong is the wrong given name.

General-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Lun of Zhao, was summoned to be general of chariots and cavalry; Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Prince Xiong of Liang, was made general-in-chief who conquers the west and area commander for military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces, garrisoning within the passes.

General-in-chief who conquers the west, Prince Lun of Zhao, was summoned to be general of chariots and cavalry; Grand Guardian of the Heir Apparent, Prince Rong of Liang, was made general-in-chief who conquers the west and area commander for military affairs in Yong and Liang provinces, garrisoning within the passes.
梁王肜 is Rong, not Xiong.
Xiahou Jun and Zhou Chu were sent against Qi Wannian in the eleventh month while Prince Xiong of Liang held a supporting camp at Haozhi.
Xiahou Jun and Zhou Chu were sent against Qi Wannian in the eleventh month while Prince Rong of Liang held a supporting camp at Haozhi.
梁王肜 is Rong; Xiong is a mistranslation of the same prince.

In the eleventh month, on the bingzi day, General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun, General Who Establishes Might Zhou Chu, and others were dispatched to attack Wannian; Prince Xiong of Liang encamped at Haozhi.

In the eleventh month, on the bingzi day, General Who Pacifies the West Xiahou Jun, General Who Establishes Might Zhou Chu, and others were dispatched to attack Wannian; Prince Rong of Liang encamped at Haozhi.
梁王肜 is Rong, not Xiong.
On the renxu day in the twelfth month Crown Prince Sima You was stripped of his title and imprisoned with his three sons in the Jinyong fortress, while his mother Lady Xie was put to death.
On the renxu day in the twelfth month Crown Prince Sima Yu was stripped of his title and imprisoned with his three sons in the Jinyong fortress, while his mother Lady Xie was put to death.
The given name 遹 is Yu, not You (攸).
On the bingzi day the young imperial grandson Sima Zang (written 𧇃 in the text) died.
On the bingzi day the imperial grandson died.
The name Sima Zang is unsupported, but the proposed text leaves the source character in an English translation.
Prince Xiong of Liang was recalled from the western command to take charge of secretariat business.
Prince Rong of Liang, general-in-chief who conquers the west, was summoned to take charge of secretariat affairs.
肜 is Rong, not Xiong; 徵 is a summons, and 征西大將軍 is the office held.
At the Ju River Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao, serving Prince Ying, routed Sun Hui’s army, which broke and ran.
At the Ju River, Zhao Xiang and Shi Chao, serving Prince Ying, routed Sun Hui’s army, which broke and ran.
The idiomatic English fuses the place Ju River with the personal name Zhao Xiang, obscuring that Zhao Xiang is a person.
On the xinyou day Wang Yu and Prince Cui of Huailing forced the palace gates, seized Sun Xiu and Prince Lun’s other confederates, and put them all to the sword.
On the xinyou day Wang Yu and Prince Cui of Huailing forced the palace gates, seized Lun’s confederates Sun Xiu, Sun Hui, Xu Chao, Shi Yi, Luo Xiu, and others, and put them all to the sword.
The idiomatic rendering omits the named confederates 孫會、許超、士猗、駱休 that the Chinese lists beside 孫秀.

Minister Sima Cui framed the decisive plot; Wang Yu, general of the left guards, with the high ministers acting in concert, led their household troops into the palace and slew Sun Xiu together with his two sons.

Minister Cui framed the decisive plot; Wang Yu, general of the left guards, with the high ministers acting in concert, led their household troops into the palace and slew Sun Xiu together with his two sons.
The idiomatic English invents the surname Sima; this sentence names only 尚書漼.
Prince Xiong of Liang was named grand steward while retaining the ministry of education on the jimao day.
Prince Rong of Liang was named grand steward while retaining the ministry of education on the jimao day.
The name 肜 is Rong here; the proposed Tong creates a new transliteration error.
That year, twelve commanderies and kingdoms drought; six locusts.
That year, twelve commanderies and kingdoms suffered drought; six had locusts.
The literal English is ungrammatical and omits the verbs implied by 旱 and 蝗.
On the dingmao day Prince Yong memorialized that Prince Jiong was plotting usurpation; he and Princes Ying, Xin, and Xiao converged on Luoyang demanding that Jiong be dismissed and sent home.

On the dingmao day Prince Yong of Hejian memorialized that Prince Jiong of Qi was plotting usurpation; together with Prince Ying of Chengdu, Prince Xin of Xinye, and Prince Xiao of Fanyang he converged on Luoyang, demanding that Jiong be dismissed and sent home.
The idiomatic English drops the territorial princely titles and fuses 成都王穎 as ‘Princes Ying’, obscuring that 穎 is a different person from Jiong’s son 英.
Sima Zhao, son of Prince Rui of Donglai, was installed as prince of Qi to replace the extirpated line.
Sima Zhao, son of Prince Rui of Donglai, was installed as prince of Qi.
The clause ‘to replace the extirpated line’ is not in the Chinese and invents a motive.
Li Te’s son Li Xiong recovered Yi Province from Jin forces in the fourth month.
In the fourth month, Li Te’s son Li Xiong again occupied Yi Province.
‘From Jin forces’ is not in the Chinese; 復據 means he again occupied the province.

In the fifth month the Yiyang chieftain Zhang Chang rebelled, set up Qiu Shen of Qiuchen as a bogus Han emperor surnamed Liu with reign Shenfeng, overran towns, and killed Prefect Liu Bin, General Yang Yi, and Prince Xin of Xinye.

In the fifth month the Yiyang chieftain Zhang Chang rebelled, set up Qiu Shen of Shandu as a bogus Han emperor surnamed Liu with reign Shenfeng, overran towns, and killed Prefect Liu Bin, General Yang Yi, and Prince Xin of Xinye.
山都 is Shandu, not Qiuchen.

In the fifth month, Yiyang Man Zhang Chang raised troops in rebellion, taking Qiuchen man Qiu Shen as lord, changing the surname to Liu, false title Han, era inception Shenfeng; he broke commanderies and prefectures; Nanyang Prefect Liu Bin, General Who Pacifies the South Yang Yi, and General-in-chief Who Guards the South, Prince Xin of Xinye, together met harm and died.

In the fifth month, Yiyang Man Zhang Chang raised troops in rebellion, taking Shandu man Qiu Shen as lord, changing the surname to Liu, false title Han, era inception Shenfeng; he broke commanderies and prefectures; Nanyang Prefect Liu Bin, General Who Pacifies the South Yang Yi, and General-in-chief Who Guards the South, Prince Xin of Xinye, together met harm and died.
山都 is Shandu, not Qiuchen.
Feng Yun of Linhuai rose in support of Zhang Chang and marched from Fuling into Xu Province.
Feng Yun of Linhuai raised troops in response to him and marched from Fuling into Xu Province.
Chinese 應之 continues from Shi Bing’s Yang campaign; the idiomatic English invents an explicit Zhang Chang object.
By the jisi day the imperial camp had withdrawn to the Xuanyang parade ground.
By the jisi day the imperial camp had withdrawn to the Xuanwu parade ground.
Chinese 宣武場 is the Xuanwu drill ground; Xuanyang is a wrong transcription of 宣武.
On the jisi day the emperor wheeled the army back to the Xuanyang drill ground.
On the jisi day the emperor wheeled the army back to the Xuanwu drill ground.
Chinese 宣武場 is Xuanwu, not Xuanyang.
At dawn on the bingshen new moon Chen Zhen of the right guards tricked the whole bureaucracy into the hall and launched a coup against Prince Ying.

On the bingshen new moon of autumn’s seventh month, General of the Right Guards Chen Zhen used an edict to summon the hundred officials into the palace hall, then led troops against Prince Ying of Chengdu.
The Chinese 以詔召 is summoning by edict, not a trick, and 勒兵討 is leading troops to attack, not an invented 'coup'.

Prince Ying’s compound already displayed the nine-summons regalia; the prince of Chenliu sent the full accoutrements of investiture, and on the following day the emperor entered Ye with complete state panoply, attended only by Prince Chi, Wang Rong, and Xun Fan.

Prince Ying’s compound already displayed the nine-bestowal regalia; the prince of Chenliu sent the full accoutrements of investiture, and on the following day the emperor entered Ye with complete state panoply, attended only by Prince Chi, Wang Rong, and Xun Fan.
九錫 is the nine bestowals, not 'nine-summons'.
An old farmer gave him a steamed fowl, which he gratefully accepted.
An old man presented a steamed chicken, which the emperor accepted.
老父 is an old man/fatherly elder, not specifically a farmer, and 受之 does not say 'gratefully'.
At Xin’an a frostbit ride threw him from his horse; Gao Guang of the ministry of the household gave him a face-wrap and earned the emperor’s praise.
At Xin’an it was bitterly cold; the emperor fell from a horse and injured his foot; Secretariat official Gao Guang presented a face-cloth, and the emperor praised him.
尚書 is a secretariat minister, not the ministry of the household; the Chinese also states the injured foot.
Gong Sifan and other officers of Prince Ying plundered the north, slew Li Zhi and Zhang Yan, and besieged Ye until Duke Mo’s general Zhao Xiang broke them.

Gongshi Fan and other officers of Prince Ying of Chengdu gathered a host, stormed commanderies, killed Yangping Prefect Li Zhi and Ji Prefect Zhang Yan, and turned to attack Ye until Duke Mo of Pingchang’s general Zhao Xiang defeated them.
公師 is the compound surname Gongshi, not Gong plus given name Sifan; the idiomatic line also drops the prefect titles and Chengdu/Pingchang designations present in the Chinese.

Subordinates of Prince Ying of Chengdu such as Gong Sifan gathered a host, stormed commanderies and prefectures, killed Yangping Prefect Li Zhi, Ji Prefect Zhang Yan, and others, then turned to attack Ye; Duke Mo of Pingchang sent General Zhao Xiang to defeat them.

Subordinates of Prince Ying of Chengdu such as Gongshi Fan gathered a host, stormed commanderies and prefectures, killed Yangping Prefect Li Zhi, Ji Prefect Zhang Yan, and others, then turned to attack Ye; Duke Mo of Pingchang sent General Zhao Xiang to defeat them.
公師藩 should be romanized Gongshi Fan because 公師 is a two-character surname.
On the gengyin new moon Gong Sifan killed Wang Jing and Feng Xiong.
On the gengyin new moon Gongshi Fan killed Pingyuan Prefect Wang Jing and Qinghe Prefect Feng Xiong.
Same surname error as s0309; the Chinese also names the two prefectures omitted in the idiomatic sentence.
On the gengyin new moon of the ninth month, Gong Sifan again killed Pingyuan Prefect Wang Jing and Qinghe Prefect Feng Xiong.
On the gengyin new moon of the ninth month, Gongshi Fan again killed Pingyuan Prefect Wang Jing and Qinghe Prefect Feng Xiong.
公師藩 should be romanized Gongshi Fan.
Zhang Fang was named supreme commander at the head of one hundred thousand men, with Lü Lang, Qian Chu, and Diao Mo among his van, to join the Xuchang operation against Liu Yu and his kin.”

Now the right general Zhang Fang is sent as supreme commander, leading one hundred thousand picked troops, with General Who Establishes Martiality Lü Lang, General of Broad Martiality Qian Chu, General Who Establishes Might Diao Mo, and others as the vanguard, to meet together at Xuchang and remove Yu and his brothers.
The literal English duplicates the idiomatic compression and misses 右將軍, 精卒十萬, the three van titles, 共會許昌, and 除輿兄弟; 將車 in the Chinese is the office 將軍.
Wang Kan of the northern camp was to strike Liu Yu’s faction.
General of the Northern Gentlemen of the Household Wang Chan was to strike Liu Yu and the others.
王闡 is Wang Chan (闡), not Kan, and 北中郎將 is an office, not merely “the northern camp.”

General of the Northern Gentlemen of the Household Wang Chan shall attack Yu and the others.
The given name 闡 corresponds to Chan, not Kan.

Yong dispatched Hongnong Prefect Peng Sui and Beidi Prefect Diao Mo to block Qi Hong and the others at Hu.

On the renchen day Qi Hong and others battled Che Diaomo; Mo was greatly defeated; Yong and Ying fled to the southern mountains and ran to Wan.
